newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bundesbank holds interest rates unchanged.
newsitem.headline: Bundesbank holds interest rates unchanged.

text.p: The Bundesbank said on Thursday its policy-making council had decided to leave the German discount and Lombard rates unchanged after its regular meeting.
The German discount rate remains at 2.50 percent and the Lombard emergency financing rate at 4.50 percent. The central bank's main money market rate, the repo, was also held steady at three percent.

Economists had generally agreed that a cut in the bank's leading interest rates was extremely unlikely. In a Reuter poll conducted this week, all 10 economists polled said they expected the discount and Lombard rates to remain unchanged.
The bank's main money market rate, the securities repurchase rate or repo, has been held steady at three percent, the rate which has prevailed since August.

Economists said that although many recent signs about the economy have not been strong, gross domestic product should start to pick up soon, leaving the Bundesbank little reason to provide a stimulus with lower interest rates.
Additionally, there had been some speculation in advance of the meeting that the central bank could decide to free private repo transactions from minimum reserve requirements at the meeting.
Many economists expect a decision on this by year-end, but there was no announcement of such plans on Thursday.
